item.content:encoded:
How much is HBO Max’s 2026 Black Friday deal?

Starting today, new and returning subscribers can lock in HBO Max (Basic with Ads) for just $5.49 per month for 12 months (regularly $10.99). That cuts the monthly price in half and saves you $66 over the year. And don’t wait — this deal ends on November 30, 2026. You can claim this promo directly through HBO Max, or snag it as an add-on through Amazon Prime Video if you like keeping your streaming subs under one roof. The discount is the same either way. And I wasn’t lying in the title — this is the best Black Friday deal I’ve seen so far for streaming services. Still, I’ll admit, this promo isn’t quite as impressive as last year’s HBO Max Black Friday deal, which dropped this exact plan down to just $2.99/mo. (!) for a full year. Between inflation and streaming price hikes (which HBO surprisingly didn’t participate in this year), paying double last year’s deal stings a little. Even so, it’s the first Black Friday streaming deal I’ve found that lasts a full 12 months. Most streamers are only offering two or six-month-long discounts this season, so I was pleasantly surprised to see this one lasts a year. A bummer it’s only on the ad-supported plan, but that’s to be expected given HBO’s previous offers. Not interested in HBO Max? Keep reading for more Black Friday streaming deals for 2026.

item.title: This Year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Will Look a Lot Different for Broadway Fans
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Wondering which Broadway shows you’ll be able to watch this Thanksgiving at the parade? Macy’s is mixing things up with an unprecedented medley of all-time favorites.
item.content:encoded:
Broadway shirks tradition for the 100th parade

As a passionate former theater kid, I always look forward to the beginning of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade — the part of the show when the parade hasn’t quite reached the cameras yet, and Broadway actors come together to entertain the TV audience while we wait. It’s a great way to get a taste of new Broadway shows when you can’t travel to New York to see them all. Last year, the parade showcased numbers from “Buena Vista Social Club,” “Just in Time,” and “Ragtime.” However, this year’s performance won’t highlight individual songs from new shows like usual. Instead, the companies of several long-running shows (and some new ones) will come together to sing a single Broadway medley. That’s a pretty big change, but I’m open to it. Let’s go over everything we know right now.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Which Broadway shows are performing at the parade?

This year’s Broadway performance will be a 10-minute medley performed by the casts of nine Broadway shows. Those shows are:

  • “Wicked”
  • “Chicago”
  • “Hamilton”
  • “The Book of Mormon”
  • “Aladdin”
  • “Schmigadoon!”
  • “The Lost Boys”
  • “The Rocky Horror Show”
  • “Rent”

Two of these, “Schmigadoon!” and “The Lost Boys,” are new shows. “Schmigadoon!” is based on the hit Apple TV show and follows a couple of lost hikers who end up in a bizarre, magical town where everyone communicates through song and dance. “The Lost Boys” is based on the cult classic ’80s film of the same name. It’s about goth, Californian vampires with cool hair and leather jackets.

The rest are all classic musicals. (The most recent, “Hamilton,” premiered over a decade ago). During normal years, the parade only highlights a few new musicals, and very rarely does it ever show songs from long-running favorites. So this medley gives more musical casts time in the spotlight — even if that time is shorter than usual. You can catch the performance at 8:30 a.m., right at the top of the parade broadcast, in all time zones.

Where to watch the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade

Peacock

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade airs on NBC, which means you can also watch it with Peacock Premium or Peacock Premium Plus.

item.title: Major League Volleyball Lands ESPN, NBC Sports in Landmark Media Deal
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: A landmark Major League Volleyball media deal brings 140 matches to four partners during the 2027 indoor season, including ESPN and NBC Sports.
item.content:encoded:
MLV adds NBC Sports and ESPN as media partners for 2027 season

One telltale sign that a sport is gaining popularity is more media coverage, whether that’s TV, print, digital, or social. One of the country’s professional women’s indoor volleyball leagues just reached that milestone. Major League Volleyball announced Tuesday that it added ESPN and NBC Sports as media partners. That expands the number of partners to four, including CBS Sports and Scripps Sports/ION. “This is a watershed moment for Major League Volleyball,” MLV Commissioner Jaime Weston said in a statement. “We have an incredible opportunity to introduce our sport to a much wider audience of sports fans, and this media lineup allows us to do exactly that. “It reflects the momentum behind women’s volleyball and the opportunity ahead of us. We are building a league that fans can follow week after week, and this is a major step forward in our growth.” The 2027 MLV season begins on Jan. 7, 2027. Five new teams joined the league ahead of the new season, bringing the total to 12.

Want more TV sports coverage?

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest event-viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

MLV matches will air throughout the week

Fans of Major League Volleyball will see dedicated nights with matches shown on specific networks, plus coverage throughout the week from the remaining partners. Here’s a quick breakdown of the slate.

  • ESPN networks will air at least 91 matches on weekends and weeknights not covered by other networks. The MLV Draft on Monday, Nov. 23, will stream on ESPN+ and the ESPN app.
  • Scripps Sports Network and ION will carry 18 matches, including 15 during primetime on Friday nights. Coverage shifts to ION after All-Star weekend. ION will again air the league semifinals and finals exclusively.
  • Peacock Premium will stream 16 matches on Thursday nights. One match will air on NBC on April 11, 2027.
  • CBS Sports Network will broadcast 10 matches during the 2027 season. CBS will air — and Paramount+ will stream — the MLV All-Star Match on March 27, 2027.

A total of 140 matches will air across networks of the four media partners — a league record.

CableTV.com analysis: MLV becomes the most widely distributed pro volleyball league in the U.S.

Major League Volleyball and League One Volleyball (LOVB) are competing for audiences in the growing U.S. women’s professional indoor volleyball market. Athletes Unlimited has also operated its own professional volleyball league, but it’s currently on pause. But with the news that MLV expanded its media rights deal, its distribution footprint is now the one to chase. Athletes Unlimited came to a three-year distribution agreement with ESPN in October 2025. Before its basketball and volleyball leagues paused, ESPN networks were slated to air only 24 games of each sport per year. LOVB currently has a multi-year distribution deal with Versant, which acquired the rights from ESPN. It also had an agreement with Victory+, but that service shut down earlier this year. It remains to be seen which media company replaces Victory+. MLV standing alone as the most widely distributed pro volleyball league in the U.S. is significant because it’s now firmly on the map compared to the other two leagues. In media these days, eyeballs matter more than anything. And if MLV teams have the most viewers, that helps improve the perception of the league.

item.title: Fubo is Becoming More Similar to Hulu + Live TV as Disney Consolidates Its Streaming Services
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Fubo customers are getting two free streaming services added to their plans. But are Disney+ and Hulu worth the recent price increase?
item.content:encoded:
Every Disney service, one subscription

Historically, we haven’t been too impressed with Fubo as a live TV streaming service. Given the choice between Fubo and Hulu + Live TV, our experts usually pick Hulu + Live TV.

But both services are owned by the same company — at least, they are as of October 2025 when the Walt Disney Company acquired a majority stake — and that company just sweetened the pot. Pro and Elite Fubo subscribers will receive a complementary subscription to the ad-supported Disney+/Hulu bundle, a $12.99 monthly value.

This all comes as Disney works to consolidate its streaming business. Hulu + Live TV is supposed to fully integrate into the Disney+ app next month, although there’s still no confirmation on when Disney will retire Hulu as a separate app and brand.

And then there’s Fubo. Rather than combining Fubo and Hulu + Live TV, as many expected when the deal closed last year, Disney is simply making Fubo a little more similar to Hulu + Live TV. For years, getting a free Disney Bundle was Hulu + Live TV’s perk alone. But now Fubo is offering the same deal.

So how much will this new bundle cost? Should you stick with Fubo, or switch to Hulu + Live TV? Let’s dive into everything we know right now.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

What streaming services do you get with Fubo?

Fubo is giving free Disney+ and Hulu (With Ads) to all of its Pro and Elite subscribers.

These aren’t the first streaming services to get added to the Fubo bundle. Last year, the company added ESPN Unlimited and FOX One (two other Disney-owned services) to the fold. So Fubo subscribers now get four on-demand streaming services at no additional cost.

Fubo’s marketing calls this a $75 value, although that’s not quite true. Thanks to the Disney Bundle, you can get Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Unlimited (With Ads) for $35.99/mo., and you can subscribe to FOX One separately for $19.99/mo. That means the true value of this bundle is $55.98/mo.

“No additional cost” may be pushing it, too — Fubo just raised its prices by $15/mo. in July. The price of the two new services, Disney+ and Hulu, combined costs $12.99/mo. So this would have been a lot better deal a year ago. But with July’s price increase also came access to NBC and Telemundo, so it wasn’t completely without merit.

Which Fubo plans are getting the Disney Bundle?

Plan Price Streaming bundle?
Pro $88.99/mo. ✔
Elite $98.99/mo. ✔

Which is a better deal, Fubo or Hulu + Live TV?

Plan Price Disney? Hulu? ESPN Unlimited? ESPN Select? FOX One?
Fubo Pro $88.99/mo. ✔ ✔ ✔ — ✔
Fubo Elite $98.99/mo. ✔ ✔ ✔ — ✔
Hulu + Live TV, Disney+, and ESPN Select $99.99/mo. ✔ ✔ — ✔ —
Hulu Premium + Live TV, Disney+ Premium, and ESPN Select $109.99/mo. ✔ ✔ — ✔ —
Looking at this table of live TV streaming bundles, Fubo’s advantage becomes clear. Hulu + Live TV is only available bundled with ESPN Select, but Fubo comes with the more feature-rich ESPN Unlimited. So if you’re a sports fan, it might be a deal worth considering. The same goes for FOX One — although I should mention that FOX One offers a separate bundle with ESPN Unlimited for $39.99/mo.

The other difference here is that both Fubo Pro and Fubo Elite come with ad-supported versions of Disney+ and Hulu. With Hulu + Live TV, you can customize your plan and banish ads from your life forever for an additional $10/mo. I’m personally using the ad-supported versions right now, and man, are they annoying while trying to catch up on the last few years of Marvel movies.

Of course, the services at the heart of both of these deals are Fubo and Hulu + Live TV. You should probably make sure the core service is actually good before letting the add-ons sway your decision. Our experts found that Hulu + Live TV has the better channel lineup, which is why we named it our Editor’s Choice in 2026. So before making any decisions, you should check out our Fubo and Hulu + Live TV reviews.

item.content:encoded:
Which streaming services are on sale for Black Friday?

Streaming prices have been climbing all year, so Black Friday is the best time to give your budget a break and take advantage of the deals these services are slinging. I mean, between corporate greed and relentless inflation, a few bucks off is the least they can do! Right on time, Amazon kicked off its official Black Friday sale today with big discounts on its Prime Video streaming add-ons. Amazon is cutting prices pretty significantly, including over half off Apple TV and a whopping 80% off both Paramount+ plans. As CableTV.com’s deals editor, keeping tabs on holiday promos is literally my job, and I’m pretty pumped to see ad-free tiers and multi-month discounts in the mix this year. Usually, providers stick to discounts on their lower-tier, ad-supported plans, so this is a big plus in my book. Check this list below for some of the best Amazon Prime Black Friday streaming deals for 2026.

  • Apple TV: $6.99/mo. for 6 months (regularly $14.99/mo.)
  • BritBox: Standard plan for $2.75/mo. for 2 months (regularly $10.99/mo.) or Premier annual plan for $124.99/yr. (regularly $149.99/yr.)
  • Crunchyroll: Fan plan for $3.99/mo. for 6 months (regularly $9.99/mo.) or Mega Fan plan for $5.99/mo. for 6 months (regularly $13.99/mo.)
  • MGM+: $1.99/mo. for 2 months (regularly $7.99/mo.) or $30.99/yr. for the annual plan (regularly $61.99/yr.)
  • Paramount+: Essential (with ads) for $2.99/mo. for 2 months (regularly $8.99/mo.) or Premium (ad-free) for $2.99/mo. for 2 months (regularly $13.99/mo.)
  • STARZ: $2.99/mo. for 2 months (regularly $11.99/mo.) or $34.99/yr. for the annual plan (regularly $69.99/yr.)

Keep in mind that because these are Prime Video add-ons, you’ll need an Amazon Prime membership (or standalone Prime Video subscription) to claim them. Plus, all plans will renew at their regular rate once the promo period is over, so set a reminder before time’s up so you don’t forget to cancel!

Of the deals I’ve mentioned, I can confirm the following providers also offer them on their standalone websites/apps: Apple TV, Crunchyroll, BritBox, MGM+, Paramount+.

STARZ‘s deals are actually better on its own website than on Amazon, offering $2.99/mo. for three months instead of two, plus its annual plan for only $12 for the whole year. That annual deal is $23 cheaper than Amazon’s offer, so if you want STARZ, skip the add-on and go straight to the STARZ app. Crunchyroll’s Fan and Mega fans are identical on Amazon and Crunchyroll.com, but if you want a discount on the top-tier Ultimate Fan plan ($8.99/mo. for six months instead of $17.99/mo.), you’ll need to sign up directly through Crunchyroll. item.title: T-Mobile Is Giving Away Free iPhone 18 Pros for Black Friday — Even If You Don’t Have a Phone to Trade In
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: T-Mobile is giving away a free iPhone 18 Pro with no trade-in required for Black Friday. See how to claim the $1,200 holiday deal and check the T-Mix plan fine print.
item.content:encoded:
Want a free iPhone? T-Mobile’s got you covered

With Black Friday right around the corner, wireless carriers are pulling out all the stops to win over holiday shoppers thinking about switching. T-Mobile’s newest Black Friday cell phone deal is no slouch. Right now, new customers can score a brand-new Apple iPhone 18 Pro on T-Mobile without having to trade in an old device, saving $1,200 off retail. As CableTV.com’s resident deals editor, I’m always skeptical of no-cost flagship phone offers. These deals often have sneaky fine print and other caveats that make the “free” phone cost you more in the long run. But I’m pleased T-Mobile is skipping the trade-in requirements on this one, since a worse trade-in can often mean less money off your supposedly free phone — and you’ll have no worries about that trickery with this deal. Still, this promo requires switching to one of T-Mobile’s new T-Mix plans and committing to a three-year payment window, so keep reading for details on how to claim this early T-Mobile Black Friday offer — and whether T-Mobile’s new plan structure is even worth the switch.

Hook it up with the hottest in TV and internet

Stay tuned for the latest deals, show premieres, and more by signing up for our newsletter.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

How to claim your free iPhone 18 Pro from T-Mobile

To get the iPhone 18 Pro (256 GB) for free, you’ll need to check off a few requirements when signing up:

  • Switch and bring your number: You need to be a new T-Mobile customer activating a new line and transferring an existing phone number from an eligible competitor like AT&T or Verizon.
  • Sign up for a qualifying T-Mix plan: You’ll need to enroll in a plan starting at $95/mo. that includes at least three “Picks,” which you’ll have to dedicate to the device promo for the duration of the finance agreement.
  • Stick around for 36 months: Heads up — before you sign up, be ready to stick with T-Mobile for three years to get the full device refund, as T-Mobile covers the $1,200 phone cost through 36 monthly bill credits.

Looking for more holiday discounts? See the latest ways to save in our guide to T-Mobile deals and promotions, or browse our main hub for the best Black Friday deals across every major internet, TV, and streaming provider.

What is T-Mobile T-Mix?

If you’re unfamiliar with T-Mobile’s new T-Mix plans, here’s the rundown. T-Mix is the name for T-Mobile’s new customizable wireless plans that skip fixed promos in favor of quarterly “Picks.” T-Mix plans let you swap out plan benefits like Netflix, Hulu, XBOX Game Pass, and device promos every three months. On paper, this flexibility is awesome if you hate paying for pre-bundled streaming services that you never use. However, in my deep dive, I noticed that the consensus among long-time T-Mobile customers on r/tmobile was overwhelmingly negative. Many Redditors argue that the new plans strip away much of T-Mobile’s built-in value, making free phone promos far less valuable than they used to be. My take: Just do your research before signing up. Start with our T-Mobile guide to get the rundown and see if making the switch to T-Mobile is worth it.

item.title: The James Gunn Era is Over, Says Newly Merged Skydance: What Does This Mean for DC Fans?
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: James Gunn has only run DC Studios for a few years, and he’s already stepping down. What does that mean for the future of Skydance and the DCEU?
item.content:encoded:
Is the DCEU getting another reboot? It’s unclear.

Last month, when Paramount Skydance merged with Warner Bros. Discovery to become just Skydance, we reported that James Gunn and Peter Safran would stay on as the heads of DC Studios. That’s because Skydance’s CEO David Ellison announced that very thing: Amid shakeups in other leadership positions, the production team behind DC superhero movies would remain the same. But it looks like Skydance is walking that statement back, because Skydance just gave the filmmaking duo the boot. The circumstances around that decision are unclear, though some blame the DC Extended Universe (DCEU)’s failure to rival the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU)’s box-office numbers. Gunn also posted a statement on Instagram in response to the news, expressing some relief and saying that he prefers being a director to being a studio head. So what does this mean for the DCEU’s future? Can Skydance ever hope to compete with Disney’s MCU empire, even as the MCU’s own numbers suffer from superhero fatigue? Am I the only person watching Marvel’s “VisionQuest?” Keep reading, and we’ll talk about it.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Relive Gunn’s DC Studios lineup

Before we speculate on the future, let’s look at DC’s recent past. Gunn and Safran took over DC Studios in 2022, when the studio (formerly DC Films) was in a pretty messy state. The merger between WarnerMedia and Discovery, Inc. put David Zaslav in charge, and he made many controversial choices. One of them was shelving “Batgirl” and “Coyote vs. ACME,” two movies that were basically completed and discarded as a tax write-off. Enter James Gunn and Peter Safran. The director/producer duo found success with “The Suicide Squad” (2021) and “Peacemaker” (2022), and Warner Bros. Discovery hoped they could reboot the DCEU into something cohesive, comprehensible, and most of all, profitable. Here’s the full list of projects from the Gunn/Safran era if you’re looking to catch up:

  • “The Suicide Squad” (2021) (under DC Films)
  • “Peacemaker” (2022–2025)
  • “Creature Commandos” (2024)
  • “Superman” (2025)
  • “Supergirl” (2026)
  • “Lanterns” (2026)
  • “Clayface” (2026)

“Superman” was a critical and commercial success, but DC Studios failed to make lightning strike twice with “Supergirl” the following year. “Clayface” made less money than “Supergirl,” but was considered a success due to its lower budget. I’d say the lesson there is probably “shrink your budget and lower your expectations,” but Skydance seems to think it needs a clean slate instead. It does have a newly merged media empire to maintain, after all. Gunn and Safran are still working on “Superman: Man of Tomorrow,” which comes out next year.

The future of DC Studios and the DCEU

So who will replace Gunn and Safran as head of DC Studios? Skydance picked Jeremy Latcham, a former Marvel executive. While at Marvel, Latcham produced “Iron Man,” “The Avengers,” and “Spider-Man: Homecoming,” as well as James Gunn’s “Guardians of the Galaxy.” Ellison praised Latcham for helping “define the modern superhero movie,” clearly hoping some of that Marvel magic will transfer over to DC. Skydance isn’t canceling any in-progress DC Studios projects, so you can still look forward to “The People v. Gorilla Grodd” and Matt Reeves’ “The Batman: Part II.” DC won’t be making the “Batgirl” mistake twice. But beyond 2027’s releases, it’s unclear what Latcham’s vision for the company will be. Four months ago, before his appointment was made public, Latcham gave an interview to Christian Broadcasting News, saying he produced the early Marvel movies with his grandma as his target demographic. If his grandma liked a movie, he reasoned, it would resonate with a wide audience. That mindset seems at odds with Gunn’s vision for the DC brand, which just produced the low-budget horror title “Clayface” this year. This could mean an end to the dark-and-edgy tone that’s defined certain DC movies since Zack Snyder was in the driver’s seat. But if Ellison is trying to copy the MCU, he certainly picked a producer with the right filmography to make it happen. If this gambit doesn’t work out, DC might just have to give up on the idea of a cinematic universe — or accept that it had the perfect cinematic universe in the Arrowverse, but threw it away during the Discovery merger. No, I’m not still salty about the “Legends of Tomorrow” cliffhanger cancellation. Why do you ask?

In this article

HBO Max

HBO Max is currently home to most DC movies. Beginning in 2027, you’ll be able to bundle it with Paramount+.

Paramount+

Paramount+ is more Transformers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles than superheroes, so you won’t find any DC titles there. But that’s just the current state of affairs — Paramount+ is expected to bundle and eventually merge with HBO Max in the next couple of years.
